title: Redwood discovery - model selection (Arcadia Labs)
summary: Initial model-selection discovery for Arcadia Labs evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key needs: 64k+ context for long legal/medical docs, strong multilingual (FR/DE/JA) support, tool-calling (fetching internal API + RAG connectors), and strict data residency/KMS requirements. Discussed open model candidates (Llama-3 variants, Mistral, Falcon/Mosaic) and tradeoffs in latency vs cost. Agreed next steps: send model-performance spreadsheet, dedicated sizing/pricing, SOC2 + KMS docs, and schedule benchmark run (pilot).
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private (KMS, VPC, audit)
next_steps: Michael to send model performance spreadsheet + recommended model shortlist by 2027-07-22
Priya to propose Dedicated sizing and cost estimate by 2027-07-24
Customer to share sample redaction-safe dataset for 1-week benchmarking run (s3 link) by 2027-07-26
Schedule technical POC kickoff (SE-led) for week of 2027-07-31
action_items: Michael Chen - Send pricing + Dedicated sizing spreadsheet - 2027-07-22
Priya Rao - Prepare benchmark plan (64k context, multilingual prompts, tool-calling flows) - 2027-07-24
Daniel Park - Provide sample documents + define success metrics (latency, exact-match QA, hallucination tolerances) - 2027-07-26
Omar Reyes - Confirm network requirements and whether Private VPC/on-prem required - 2027-07-26
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-19 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Michael (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (CTO, Arcadia), Sarah (ML Eng), Omar (Infra)
[00:00] Michael: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Michael Chen from Redwood. How's it going?
[00:06] Daniel: Good, thanks. We got a few people here, uh Sarah and Omar. We're excited to talk models.
[00:10] Michael: Great. Quick agenda: understand your workloads, context length, multilingual needs, tool-calling, and then run through hosted vs dedicated vs private. Priya will cover the technicals.
[00:20] Priya: Hi all — quick note, I'll jump into perf tradeoffs and kernel stuff when we discuss quantization + batching.
[00:28] Sarah: To start, our primary use case is document Q&A across legal and medical records, lots of long docs, we need 60k-100k-ish context for multi-doc ops. Also need French/German/Japanese support.
[00:40] Michael: Ok 60k-100k, noted. Are you leaning open models or are you considering hosted closed models too?
[00:46] Daniel: Prefer open models for cost and control, but we also care about tool-calling for internal APIs and RAG connectors. We want function-calls or similar.
[00:55] Priya: Redwood supports tool-calling patterns — our streaming + function calling works with variants of open models; some models implement function semantics better than others. There's also difference in context window handling, some require chunking + RAG.
[01:05] Sarah: For multilingual, we've had mixed results with Mistral on JA; Llama-3 did well in our quick tests but cost was high.
[01:12] Omar: Security-wise, we must be SOC2 compliant, keys in our KMS, and data residency in EU for a subset of customers. If Private is required, we'd need VPC + HSM integration.
[01:22] Michael: That's pretty standard. Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. For Hosted we offer bring-your-own-KMS in select enterprise tiers, but Dedicated or Private gives more control.
[01:34] Daniel: Can you summarize cost differences? Long context models and 64k windows sound expensive.
[01:38] Michael: Sure — rough buckets: Hosted with smaller open models (quantized) is cheapest per-token but may need more RAG chunking, which adds latency. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost for high volume. Private is highest due to infra but required for strict compliance. We'll send a dedicated sizing/pricing.
[01:55] Priya: Technically, for 64k context we often recommend models that natively support long-context or offload to KV cache / segmented attention — Llama-3-long variants, Mistral long-context forks, or specialized 128k models. There's also tradeoffs: quantized models (4-bit) reduce memory but impact some quality in instruction-following.
[02:12] Sarah: What's Redwood's stance on kernel selection and latency? We saw big variance across hw.
[02:18] Priya: Our runtime does kernel selection per model + per-sequence-length profile. For shorter requests we prioritize latency-optimized kernels; for long context we pick memory-optimized paths. We also do continuous batching, prefix cache (KV cash in some transcripts) to reduce per-token cost.
[02:33] Omar: Any restrictions on tool-calling for Private? We need to call internal APIs behind our network.
[02:38] Michael: With Private you can run the control plane on Redwood and the runtime inside your VPC, or go fully on-prem. Tool-calling flows can be proxied via your network, function calls execute in your environment if you want.
[02:50] Daniel: Ok, model candidates — what are you recommending for our mix of long context + FR/DE/JA?
[02:55] Priya: Recommendation shortlist: 1) Llama-3 large-long (good generalist, strong multilingual when finetuned), 2) Mistral-Instruct long-context branch (very competitive on latency/throughput), 3) MosaicML/Falcon long-window variants (good performance and cost), 4) Smaller distilled models for cheap embedding/lookup tiers. We'll attach perf numbers.
[03:18] Sarah: Are there big differences in hallucination with 64k context? We worry about drift across multi-doc QA.
[03:23] Priya: Hallucination often comes from RAG retrieval quality and prompt engineering; longer context can help but also introduce distractors. We recommend structured prompts + grounding, and Redwood Optimize can detect regressions via evals tied to prompt-sets.
[03:38] Michael: Also worth noting: for extremely strict accuracy we run a reranker / verifier step — some customers run a smaller verifier model post-generation to check citations. That adds latency but reduces hallucination.
[03:48] Omar: Network/infra questions: if we run Dedicated in a cloud region, can we force traffic to eu-west-1 only?
[03:55] Michael: Yes, region pinning and smart routing policies exist — can route by region/customer tier. Private is of course fully under your network control.
[04:03] Daniel: What's the expected latency for 64k context for a single-doc summarize?
[04:07] Priya: Ballpark: hosted with quantized model ~2-6s per 1k tokens for generation heavy ops; with 64k you'll see higher tail latency due to attention paths. Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching can reduce per-token latency and cost; exact numbers depend on hardware (A100 vs H100 vs newer). We'll run benchmarks against your dataset.
[04:25] Sarah: Tool-calling specifics: we need function calling to run search over our internal vector DB, then call internal API to fetch the canonical doc and redact PII before sending to model. Does Redwood have recommended patterns?
[04:35] Priya: Yes — typical flow: 1) client queries vector DB -> 2) fetch doc -> 3) run redact step (in your infra) -> 4) pass redacted doc to model. You can implement both 2/3 inside your network; Redwood's runtime can orchestrate calls but for Private we recommend keeping fetch/redact inside your VPC for compliance.
[04:55] Michael: We'll include a sample architectural diagram in the follow-up deck (link: https://redwood.example/decks/arcadia-poc).
[05:03] Daniel: Are there any models that support function-calling natively so we can get deterministic structured outputs?
[05:08] Priya: Some open models have community-built function-calling wrappers; Redwood provides a function-calling shim that maps model tokens to structured JSON output, with schema validation. Behavior varies by model so part of the POC is to validate which model gives the most reliable schema adherence.
[05:25] Sarah: For multilingual, would you recommend a single multilingual model or language-specific models per pipeline?
[05:30] Priya: Single multilingual model simplifies infra but can be slightly worse on edge languages. For high-accuracy in Japanese we sometimes recommend a Japan-specialized model or finetune on local data. We'll show per-lang perf in the spreadsheet.
[05:45] Omar: Compliance: SOC2 + ISO? KMS integration — what's the typical lead time?
[05:50] Michael: Redwood is SOC2 compliant; we provide SOC2 report and ISO documentation on request. KMS integration timeline depends on whether you're using our hosted KMS integration or Private. BYOK for hosted enterprise can take a few weeks to configure; Private on-prem obviously more planning. We'll attach security docs.
[06:06] Daniel: Ok good. Let's talk about the POC scope and success criteria.
[06:10] Michael: Suggested POC: 2-week benchmarking run comparing 3 model variants across (1) latency, (2) QA exact match on sample queries, (3) token cost, (4) multilingual accuracy. Run on your sample dataset with 64k windows and tool-calling flow. Success criteria: >=85% exact-match on golden set, avg latency <5s on standard queries, and cost per query under your target which you'll provide.
[06:33] Sarah: We'll produce golden set + metrics.
[06:36] Daniel: Who owns the POC infra cost?
[06:38] Michael: Redwood typically covers an initial benchmark run for qualified opportunities; if you need dedicated hardware reserved we'll propose a short-term Dedicated commitment. We'll clarify in the follow-up.
[06:48] Omar: One more infra question: do you support HSM for key wrap?
[06:52] Michael: Yes — HSM + KMS integrations are supported in Private and in higher enterprise tiers. We'll include the KMS/HSM integration guide.
[07:00] Priya: Quick note on quantization: for 64k windows memory becomes a first-class constraint. We often run 4-bit quantized models to fit within practical GPU memory but recommend validating quality. Some workloads require 8-bit or FP16 for best quality.
[07:15] Sarah: About reranking and caching — you mentioned prefix caching earlier. Can you elaborate?
[07:20] Priya: Prefix caching stores KV states for repeated prefixes so subsequent requests that share the same prefix avoid recomputing. For multi-turn chains where the beginning is stable this saves a lot. Also we have intelligent batching to increase throughput for similar sequence profiles.
[07:35] Daniel: Any limitations on fine-tuning or instruct-tuning? We have in-house downstream finetunes.
[07:40] Michael: Redwood can serve finetuned weights; for Hosted we support customer-provided model artifacts in enterprise tiers or you can host finetuned models in Private. We'll detail how to load and version finetunes.
[07:54] Sarah: Are there SLA options on latency for Dedicated?
[07:57] Michael: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and can be configured with latency targets depending on commit levels. Details in the pricing follow-up.
[08:05] Omar: Ok, any blockers we see right now for the POC?
[08:09] Priya: Only need the sample dataset and success metrics. Also confirm whether you require EU-only hosting or Private.
[08:16] Daniel: We'll confirm residency reqs. Likely EU-only for production but POC can run in US/EU.
[08:21] Michael: Great — I'll send the model perf spreadsheet and a draft POC plan. Priya will own the technical plan.
[08:27] Sarah: Quick question on telemetry — what do we see in Redwood Console about per-route token breakdown?
[08:32] Michael: Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and tracing hooks. You can link traces to your own observability stack.
[08:40] Daniel: Good. Any potential gotchas with long-context during scaling?
[08:44] Priya: The main ops gotchas are memory capacity (GPU per-worker limits), batching behavior with long tails, and cache invalidation for KV cache. We'll help size correctly.
[08:55] Omar: We use Okta for SSO — supported?
[08:57] Michael: Yes SAML/SSO via Okta is supported, RBAC, audit logs.
[09:03] Priya: Also for the POC we recommend running a small set of structured prompts that validate tool-calling reliability — e.g., call vector DB, fetch doc, redact, pass to model, then validate structured JSON output.
[09:15] Sarah: That makes sense.
[09:18] Michael: Any other questions?
[09:20] Daniel: Not right now. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:22] Michael: Recap: Michael sends spreadsheet/pricing, Priya sends POC plan/benchmarks, Arcadia provides sample data and metrics, Omar confirms residency. We'll reconvene later this week to lock dates.
[09:33] (crosstalk) Omar: Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Michael: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:40] End of recording.
